Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing question / TPS estimates

Hey Jasmine,

Quick one — we're sizing for a pilot in Q2 and the finance team asked for a tokens/sec estimate and a recommended dedicated pool to hit our latency targets. High-level: ~750 concurrent end-users, expected average interaction rate ~1.5 requests/user/minute (roughly 11.25 rps), with an average prompt + response length we estimate at ~180 tokens per interaction. Our p95 latency target is 350ms for the critical path (inference only).

Can Redwood run a rough fit showing:
- tokens/sec (steady) and burst estimates
- minimal GPUs to hit p95 350ms vs conservative pool for 30% burst headroom
- latency sensitivity if we enable 8-bit quantization or use a smaller model variant

We're trying to decide between a 6- or 10-GPU reserved pool for the pilot. Any quick guidance would be great — happy to share access to a representative workload log if that helps.

Thanks,
Hector
AtlasOne — Head of Platform

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 11:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing question / TPS estimates — initial model

Folks — did a quick pass with the numbers Jasmine shared. Notes + assumptions first, then a table summary.

Assumptions:
- Model: open-30B variant (float16 baseline); quantized option: int8/8-bit dequant path.
- Avg tokens per interaction: 180 (30 prompt + 150 generation)
- Client steady RPS: 11.25 (750 users * 1.5 reqs/min = 1125 reqs/hour -> 11.25 rps)
- Steady tokens/sec: 11.25 * 180 = 2,025 tps.
- Burst scenario: 4x peak request load for short windows -> 45 rps -> burst tokens/sec 8,100 tps.
- Benchmarks (measured on our A100-equivalent profile):
    - float16 baseline: ~12,000 tps per GPU (large context amortization and batching)
    - int8 quantized path: ~22,000 tps per GPU (reduced memory bandwidth, more efficient kernels)

Quick sizing table (rounded):
- Baseline (steady): 2,025 tps / 12,000 tps per GPU -> 0.17 GPUs -> 1 GPU minimal to cover steady (practical: 1 always-on).
- Burst fit without quantization: 8,100 / 12,000 -> 0.675 -> still <1 GPU for pure compute, but we need headroom for concurrency, KV cache memory, and parallel requests. So recommending 3 GPUs to avoid queueing and keep p95 latency near target.
- Baseline with int8 quant: 2,025 / 22,000 -> 0.092 -> 1 GPU minimal. Burst with int8: 8,100 / 22,000 -> 0.37 -> 1 GPU.

Recommendation (practical):
- Minimal reserved pool: 3x A100-class GPUs (float16 runtime). This gives room to handle bursts and maintain batching without saturating the token pipeline. Expect p95 around 220-300ms in our synthetic runs for typical prompt lengths.
- Buffered pool (30% safety + room for KV cache and parallel user sessions): 5x GPUs. This maps to ~5 * 12k = 60k tps capacity (float16) and provides buffer for routing overhead, warming, and short sustained bursts.
- If AtlasOne accepts int8 quantized variant (quality permitting): 2x GPUs would likely be sufficient for the buffered profile; 1 GPU might suffice for minimal but we'd still recommend 2 for redundancy.

I'll attach the per-GPU run numbers I used. These assume batch sizes optimized for latency (we avoid extremely large batching to preserve p95).

—Ben
Principal Capacity Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 09:44:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing question / TPS estimates — SLA mapping

Jasmine / Ben — good notes. Adding SLA mapping and operational caveats.

SLA / SLO considerations:
- p95 target 350ms (inference only) — with 3 GPUs float16 we project p95 between 200–320ms under steady and mild bursts. Under sustained 4x bursts (tens of minutes), p95 can degrade toward 400–600ms if NVLink/host contention appears.
- Autoscaling: we should enable reserved burst capacity + fast warm pool. For pilot, recommended policy: 3 reserved GPUs, autoscale to +2 GPUs on sustained 60s+ elevated CPU/RPS thresholds. That keeps latency within SLO for most realistic bursts.
- Fallbacks: offer a lower-cost model variant knob (smaller 7B family) that can be used automatically if latency breaches are sustained; however that implies quality/regression risk and would be visible to the app as a model swap.
- Quantization risk: int8 path shows strong throughput gains but we must run an eval set for prompt fidelity. Recommend quality gate: 95% token-level parity on sampled prompt set or human-in-the-loop QC for 1000 sample responses before enabling int8 in prod.

Cost / commercial note for sales proposal:
- 3x GPU reserved baseline for pilot (with autoscale up to 5) hits the p95 target with <10% overcommit risk for expected traffic patterns.
- 5x GPU reserved (buffered) reduces risk to <2% for sustained bursts and gives room for short A/B rollouts / model variant experiments.

I’ll draft a short blurb for the proposal describing risk tolerances and the contingency steps (autoscale, model fallback, feature-flagged quantization).

—Neha
Director, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference

Hi Hector / Priya — thanks for the clear brief. Summary of the recommendation and next steps below. Please see attached CSV + short runbook for details.

Executive summary (pilot):
- Steady tokens/sec: ~2,025 tps. Burst estimate (short windows): ~8,100 tps.
- Recommendation: Reserve a 3-GPU dedicated pool (A100-class equivalent) for the pilot. Autoscale policy: add up to +2 GPUs when sustained RPS > 20 for > 60s. This configuration keeps p95 inference latency ~220–320ms in our tests, and remains comfortably under your 350ms p95 target for the expected workload.
- Alternative (lower-cost with quantization): If AtlasOne can accept an int8 quantized path after a short evaluation, a 2-GPU reserved pool with the same autoscale policy is feasible — this reduces unit cost but requires a quality validation gate.
- Buffered option (for stronger SLA/commercial commitments): 5-GPU reserved pool to reduce risk and enable experiments without capacity contention.

Operational notes:
- We will provide a short runbook describing warm-up, prefix caching, and tail-latency mitigation (attached).
- We suggest a 2-week pilot with traffic ramp from 10% -> 75% over four days while we monitor p50/p95/p99 and tune batching and cache settings.

Next steps / ask from AtlasOne:
1) Confirm which model variant you prefer for the pilot (open-30B float16 vs smaller 7B vs int8 evaluation).
2) Approve a pilot pool request (we will provision 3 GPUs; billing starts on provisioning).
3) Share a representative prompt sample (if you haven't already) so we can run the int8 parity checks quickly.

If you want, we can schedule a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through the numbers.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
